detail: `TrustManagerFactory.init(KeyStore)` documents that a null KeyStore is permitted and selects the default trust material (WEB-001). The source deliberately passes `null as KeyStore?` to use that documented platform default (TLS-CLAIM-002, TLS-CLAIM-003). An explicit keystore is not an equivalent replacement for the platform-default trust-store selection.

SSLContext.init is documented to accept a caller-supplied TrustManager[] and use it as the TLS trust policy. The original call supplies the deliberately selected DefaultTrustManager or PinningTrustManager. In particular, PinningTrustManager is the application’s documented-by-code mechanism for accepting its configured certificate while enforcing its pin and hostname checks. Replacing it with the platform-default TrustManagerFactory changes that security-relevant acceptance behavior rather than repairing misuse of SSLContext.init.
